newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
SYDNEY-TO-HOBART APPEAL DISMISSED

An unprecedented racing rules appeal, which could have upset the top overall corrected time placings of the 1996 Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart race, has been dismissed by the Yachting Association of New South Wales (YANSW) appeals committee.

Had the appeal been upheld, the fourth-placed BZW Challenge, owned by Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron member RAY ROBERTS, could have been placed first overall ahead of the provisional International Measurement System (IMS) winner, Ausmaid, owned by Melbourne yachtsman GIORGIO GJERGJA.

ROBERTS had appealed against the amount of time granted by the race jury as redress for time BZW Challenge lost in responding to the sighting of a possible distress flare in Bass Strait on the second night of the race last December.
The jury granted BZW Challenge 33 minutes time allowance instead of the two hours redress sought by ROBERTS.

In dismissing the appeal, the YANSW appeals committee decided this week that it was not satisfied there had been a misinterpretation of the rules as provided for in International Yacht Racing Rule 77.4 -- the basic ground for an appeal.

However, the committee commended BZW Challenge for promptly responding to the sighting of a flare -- not doing so could have resulted in loss of life -- and added that the fact the source of the flare could not be discovered and that the colour of the flare was white was not relevant.
The crew are to be congratulated for their efforts in trying to locate its source, the committee said.

The Cruising Yacht Club of Australia today confirmed provisional IMS overall results for the 52nd Sydney-to-Hobart as: 1. Ausmaid, GIORGIO GJERGJA, Sandringham Yacht Club, Victoria. 2. Exile, WARWICK MILLER, Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club, Hong Kong. 3. Atara, ROGER HICKMAN, Cruising Yacht Club of Australia, New South Wales. 4. BZW Challenge, RAY ROBERTS, Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron, New South Wales. 5. Bit of Fluff, WARREN BROOKS, Mackay Yacht Club, Queensland.

And everyone can keep the trophies presented at the Royal Yacht Club of Tasmania on January 2 and race director Phil Thompson can have the fine perpetual trophies, including the historic Tattersalls Cup, engraved for posterity!
ADMIRAL'S CUP CREWS IN TRAINING
Australia's Admiral's Cup team skippers and crews are already training hard for the July/August regatta at Cowes, England.

Olympic bronze medallist COLIN BEASHEL will join sailmaker and America's Cup yachtsman GRANT SIMMER and prominent Sydney yachtsman ROBIN CRAWFORD and other crew members in sailing the chartered ILC-40, G Net, in New Zealand next week. SYD FISCHER and STEVE KULMAR and their crews are maintaining the pressure on the local Sydney racing scene.
BEASHEL, SIMMER and company will sail G Net in the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron's IMS Regatta out of Auckland before having the yacht prepared for shipping to Europe.

BEASHEL, who recently won the Tag Heuer Magic 25 national championship on Pittwater, is already in New Zealand contesting that country's inaugural Etchells championship against the likes of U.S. America's Cup skippers DENNIS CONNER and PAUL CAYARD.
After a dismal performance in the Cruising Yacht Club's short offshore race two weeks ago, FISCHER cracked the whip last Saturday for an impressive win in his Farr-50, Ragamuffin.
Equally impressive was KULMAR at the helm of his Mumm-36, Sea, in placing third.

Both owners will charter yachts overseas for the Admiral's Cup but will continue training here, including contesting Middle Harbour Yacht Club's annual race to Mooloolaba on Queensland's Sunshine Coast, starting Saturday fortnight, March 22.
More than 50 yachts have entered this 470-nautical mile race, including WARWICK MILLER's Exile and CHARLES CURRAN's Sydney, with likely America's Cup challenger IAIN MURRAY at the helm.

Meanwhile, an e-mail message from the Royal Ocean Racing Club in England says that Germany, four-times winners of the Admiral's Cup, are the fourth nation to formally challenge for the Champagne Mumm Admiral's Cup, joining Australia, Great Britain and New Zealand. Up to a dozen nations are expected to field three-boat teams.
BOBSLED HEADS 49TH BRISBANE-GLADSTONE FLEET

Easter 1998 promises to be a great time for offshore yacht racing in Queensland, with the Queensland Cruising Yacht Club staging the 50th annual Easter race from Brisbane to Gladstone. In fact, enthusiasm is already building up with a strong fleet entered for this year's 49th Gladstone race.

Heading the fleet after returning to her home port is race record-holder Bobsled, the KELL STEINMANN-designed 66-footer which late last year contested the 25th Melbourne-to-Hobart Westcoaster race, finishing second astern of Melbourne yacht Future Shock.

Bobsled is now back with her owners, with part-owner and principal helmsman ROBERT BIRD looking forward to a great sail north on Good Friday, March 28. BIRD was in Bobsled's crew when she smashed the record with an extraordinary time of 21 hours 59 minutes 43 seconds for the 308-nautical mile race.

Among entries expected to be strong IMS handicap contenders are Sydney businessman RAY ROBERTS' Corel-45, BZW Challenge, Townsville yachtsman CAREY RAMM's Farr-39, No Fearr and Gold Coast surgeon GILBERT FORD's ROBERT HICK-designed 30-footer, Atria, which won its division in the recent Sydney to Hobart. ROBERTS will be looking forward to success after his disappointing Hobart race outcome mentioned above.
FIRST OF NEW WHITBREAD-60s LAUNCHED

While Australia's prospects of mounting a challenge for the 1997-98 Whitbread Round-the-World race are now virtually nil, two new yachts for New Zealander GRANT DALTON's Merit Cup Whitbread campaign were launched in Auckland this week.
The boats, the first of the new generation Whitbread-60s to be built for the race, were lifted into the water with little ceremony at the end of an intensive 18-week building programme.
The Merit Cup yachts are almost identical but only one will sail in the Whitbread race.

For skipper DALTON, who won the last Whitbread Race with the maxi ketch New Zealand Endeavour, the launching was the culmination of more than two years' work seeking sponsorship, designing and building the yachts and selecting the crew.
"It's very satisfying to have the boats in the water and having the campaign in such good shape with the start of the race still seven months away," Dalton said.

Watching the launch with special interest were American DENNIS CONNER and New Zealander CHRIS DICKSON, former America's Cup and Whitbread Race rivals and now partners in the Toshiba campaign for the Whitbread.
CONNER heads the syndicate and DICKSON will be the skipper of Toshiba.

As a grey dawn broke over Auckland, DICKSON was seen taking photographs of the two Merit Cup yachts, with a camera-shy CONNER arriving later but leaving after the local media began to focus on his spying presence.
Merit Cup skipper DALTON said he was flattered by his rivals' attention.
"I thought they were the experts on the Whitbread 60s. They sailed them in the last Whitbread. I was sailing a maxi," he commented.
GILMOUR AGAIN RUNNER-UP TO COUTTS
Australian PETER GILMOUR, now a resident of Japan in the lead-up to America's Cup 2000, has again had to accept the role of runner-up to New Zealand's winning Cup skipper, RUSSELL COUTTS.
GILMOUR and COUTTS were among a bevy of America's Cup skippers who helmed the top IMS yachts in this week's Southern Ocean Racing Conference regatta sailed in heavy weather off Miami, Florida.

GILMOUR drew first blood in the IMS1 division, steering the Japanese owned ILC-46, Swing, but at the end of the regatta it was COUTTS who came out on top with the Canadian-owned Taylor-49, Numbers, which New Zealand has chartered for this year's Admiral's Cup.
COUTTS still heads the International Sailing Federation's world match race rankings with GILMOUR number two on the list, but they haven't met on the match racing circuit since last year.
* Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800.
